headers.text: What it means for the system

rows.text: We never control the camera (no turning or zooming). We only read.
It is addressed, like a website
Only the address changes when a real CCTV replaces our stand-in. The rest of the system does not change.
Cameras get switched off and Wi-Fi drops. The system must notice, say so in words, and reconnect by itself.
The AI can be slower than the camera
If the AI needs more time than 40 ms per frame, old frames pile up and the picture falls behind. We keep only the newest.

blocks.text: Step 2: the address, and which setups we accept
blocks.kicker: How CCTV hands out its picture

inlines.text: CCTV systems from different makers all end up giving you one of a few kinds of address. We looked up the common ones and made the Live Monitor accept them. The right-hand column is honest about what we have and have not tried.

rows.text: : the standard way cameras and recorders stream
. The viewer can choose UDP, multicast or TCP delivery.
The camera offers an RTSP address

inlines.text: The Hikvision and Dahua paths agree across vendor and installer pages, but many are third-party, and ports and paths can differ by model and firmware, so the camera's own manual decides. The sources also disagree on which video format ONVIF Profile S makes mandatory, so read the ONVIF specification itself before quoting that detail.

blocks.text: Where the system decides what an address means

inlines.text: One small function,
, looks at the text and decides: a webcam number, a stream address, or a file. It refuses anything else, so a typed address can never be used to make the system open something it should not.

tokens.text: """Work out what an address is. Raises ValueError for anything that is not a file, webcam or allowed stream."""
f"Unsupported source type '{scheme}://' (use rtsp, http, rtmp or udp)"

notes.text: A plain number such as 0 means a webcam plugged into this computer.
Something like rtsp:// or http:// means a stream. The part before the // is the kind.
Only rtsp, rtsps, http, https, rtmp and udp are allowed. Any other kind is refused.
The label shown on screen hides the password: user:***@address.
A trick some video tools understand (joining or piping files) is refused on purpose.
Anything left is a video file on this computer.

blocks.text: Step 3: reading the picture without falling behind

inlines.text: is the part that talks to the camera. It has three jobs, and each one answers a problem from the first section.

items.text: Connecting to a dead address must give up after a few seconds, and tell the user.

children.text: Ask for the safe, low-delay way.

items.text: Video over UDP can lose pieces on Wi-Fi and smear the picture, so we ask for TCP and for no buffering.
A reader thread keeps taking pictures from the camera. When the AI is ready, it gets the latest one; older ones are dropped. Lag cannot pile up.
If the stream drops, wait 1, 2, 4, 8 seconds and try again, and show OFFLINE meanwhile.

blocks.title: The settings that make it safe

tokens.text: # TCP: UDP drops packets on Wi-Fi (smeared frames). No-buffer / low-delay: show frames as they arrive.
# nothing else is handed to ffmpeg

notes.text: Wait at most 5 seconds to connect.
Wait at most 5 seconds for the next picture.
After a drop, retry after 1, 2, 4, then every 8 seconds.
Ask for TCP (no smeared pictures) and low delay (show pictures as they arrive).

blocks.title: The reader loop: connect, read, reconnect

notes.text: Try to connect to the camera.
Could not connect: wait a little longer each time, then try again.
Take the next picture from the camera.
Hand it over as the newest picture.
The stream dropped: count it, show OFFLINE, and go round again.

tokens.text: # nobody took the previous frame: it is stale now

notes.text: Nobody took the previous picture, so it is old now. Count it as dropped.
Replace it with the new one, stamped with the time it arrived. That stamp gives the lag number on screen.
Wake the AI if it was waiting for a picture.

inlines.text: 31 automated tests cover this file, using a scripted fake camera (no network needed). They check what an address means, that the newest picture wins, that a silent camera gives up, that a dropped stream reconnects, and that stopping never releases a camera that is still being read.

blocks.text: Steps 4 and 5: from the AI to your screen

inlines.text: The AI loop is in
. For each picture it finds vehicles and runs the violation rules. The dashboard then needs two things: the data (boxes, tickets) and the picture. There are two ways to send the picture, chosen by
HK_PICTURE_MODE

rows.text: Boxes that sit exactly on the vehicles. No encoder and no relay to go wrong.
A bit more network and CPU per picture (fine on one computer)
Smooth video that also works for other viewers
The picture arrives later than the boxes, so the dashboard has to delay the boxes by eye

inlines.text: We first used only the relay. The picture took the longer way (encoder, relay, player) and showed up two seconds or more after the boxes, so the boxes ran ahead of the vehicles, and no fixed delay could cure it. Putting the picture in the same message makes it impossible for them to disagree.
The rest of this section is about the
mode.
In relay mode, without the relay there is no picture, so the backend starts it by itself when it is installed in
hulikamote_backend/tools/mediamtx

blocks.title: A real bug we found and fixed (worth telling the panel)

inlines.text: When the relay was
running, the encoder could not send anywhere and stopped reading. The backend kept writing pictures into it, the pipe filled up, and the
: uploads and Start hung for ever. The fix has two parts: pictures are handed to a separate writer thread through a small queue that
pictures when it is full, and stopping
the encoder first instead of waiting on it. An automated test makes a deliberately stuck encoder and checks that nothing blocks.

blocks.title: Only this thread can ever get stuck on the encoder

tokens.text: """Feeds frames to ffmpeg. Only this thread can ever block on the pipe, so a stuck encoder cannot freeze the rest."""

notes.text: Take the next waiting picture from the queue.
Write it to the encoder. This is the call that can block, so it runs in its own thread.
If the encoder is gone, mark it stopped and quit this thread.

blocks.title: Stopping never waits on a stuck encoder

tokens.text: """Stop ffmpeg. Never waits on a stuck encoder: it is killed first, because closing a pipe that nobody reads
from would wait for ever (that froze the whole backend)."""
# wakes the writer if it is idle

notes.text: Kill the encoder first. Closing a pipe that nobody reads from would wait for ever.
Only now close the pipe; it cannot block any more.
Give the writer thread one second to finish, then move on.

blocks.text: How the Live Monitor makes sure it works

inlines.text: A frozen or missing part used to look like endless loading. Now the screen checks before it starts and says what is wrong, in words:

rows.text: The backend is stopped or frozen
The backend is not answering. Restart it, then press Try again.
The video relay (MediaMTX) is not running... Then press Try again.
Connected, but no picture in 12 seconds
Connected, but no picture yet. Check the source with Change source.
Pick another source or check the camera

inlines.text: plays a video clip as if it were a camera, with the same kind of address a real one gives. Run it on the same laptop, or on a second laptop on the same hotspot.

items.text: . It reports the picture size, speed and time to the first picture. The code is

inlines.text: A phone works the same way: install an Android RTSP camera app, start it, and paste the address it shows. Use your own phone hotspot or router, not venue Wi-Fi, which often stops devices from seeing each other.

blocks.text: What we claim, and what we do not

inlines.text: We do not claim that HULI-KAMOTE works on a real barangay CCTV. We surveyed how CCTV systems usually hand out their picture, built the Live Monitor to accept those inputs, and tested the same path with stand-in cameras. A real camera needs only its address.

rows.text: Failure handling: backend down, relay missing, no picture, dropped stream, reconnect
The freeze fix, with a deliberately stuck encoder

inlines.text: Two honest limits: accuracy depends on the camera's angle and quality (blur, glare, small plates), and opening a barangay's CCTV needs their permission, the recorder's address and its password. The system only reads the picture; it has no pan, tilt, zoom or audio.
